timeline: You assume nobody predicted the Bhopal disaster, but Rajkumar Keswani published warnings beginning in 1982 before it struck in 1984.
In nineteen eighty one, his friend died inhaling phosgene inside the Union Carbide plant.
Two fired workers handed him confidential safety manuals.
He discovered toxic gases were heavier than air.
He warned that a disaster would wipe out the city.
Yet nobody paid attention to his shrill warnings.
Even his closest friends thought he was crazy.
Then the plant leaked on December third.
He became the only journalist who understood the catastrophe.
You assume nobody predicted the disaster.
